questions.question: On the night of ______ 1975, Indira Gandhi recommended the imposition of Emergency to president Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25th June**____**.**__

__
 
• The **Indian Emergency was a 21 month** period **beginning from 25th June 1975 to 21st March 1977.**
 
• **On the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**, **President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed declared a state of emergency** under **Article 352** of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution stipulates three types of emergencies-
 
 
• **National Emergency**- Under **Article 352**, the president can declare a national emergency when the security of India or a part of it is threatened by war or external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• **Constitutional Emergency**- Under** Article 356**, empowers the President to issue a proclamation if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the constitution.
 
• **Financial Emergency**- **Article 360** empowers the president to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term ‘**armed rebellion**’ is inserted from the **44th amendment**. Before this term, it was known as **an internal disturbance**.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** laid out that **Article 19 can only be suspended when the National Emergency** is laid on the grounds of war or external aggression and not in the case of armed rebellion.
 
• An emergency was declared in India in the **1962 war (China war)**, **1971 war (Pakistan war)**, and **1975 internal disturbance** (declared by Indira Gandhi).

questions.question: Iron nails become ______ after being dipped in copper sulphate solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**brownish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Metal activity series:​**

__
 
• The **metals are arranged in an activity order that is known as metal activity series.
 
• The more active metals are present at the top of the series whereas the less active metals are put at the end of the series.
 
• The metal activity series is as follows- 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f72c7124c6f6b6df6ff803bb9d21ff32167392bfbf97526a2b34b5f710d4b56.png] ​

Importance of the series-**

 
• The metal activity series is used to predict displacement reactions.
 
• When an** iron nail **is **dipped in copper sulphate **solution, a **brown coating of copper** is formed in the surface of iron and the colour of copper sulphate solution changes from blue to pale green.

**Explanation:**__

Displacement reaction

 
• It is a reaction wherein the atom or a set of atoms is displaced by another atom in a molecule.
 
• The reaction shows that** iron is more reactive than copper** because it displaces copper from the** copper sulphate **solution.

Hence, **Iron nails become brown **whereas the solution turns green.

 
• **CuSO4 (aq) + Fe (s) → FeSO4 (aq) + Cu (s)** 
 
• In this reaction following two processes take place:
 
 
• Cu²⁺ + 2e = Cu⁰ (re­duc­tion process, Cu²⁺ is the ox­i­dizing agent)
 
• Fe⁰ – 2e = Fe²⁺ (ox­i­da­tion process, Fe⁰ is the re­duc­ing agent)
 
 
 
• The reaction can be double displacement reaction as well as redox reaction (oxidation and reduction both take place simultaneously).

• The given sentence is talking about **a past habitual action.** 
 
• **Want to **denotes something that the person would like to do in the **future. **
 
• Therefor it is grammatically incorrect as the given sentence is expressing a past action. 
 
• And we know that in such cases **'used to'** should be used instead of **'want to'. **
 
• **'Used to'** is **a modal verb. **It means **done or experienced in the past, but no longer done or experienced. **
 
 
• *Example: We don’t go to the movies now as often as we **used to.***
 
 
 
• Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *I **used to** learn yoga when I was in school. *
